hyps.why: Adding a 3x3 conv on a removed edge into the output restores a feature path, which gains more than swapping one existing op for another.
Replacing a missing edge with a conv adds capacity and connectivity, a larger gain than replacing an existing op.
Edge 0 feeds nodes 1 and 2, so re-enabling it with a conv opens deeper paths and gives a large gain.
Filling an empty edge with a conv adds a learnable path, which is better than replacing an existing op with a 1x1 conv.
Removing a 3x3 conv from the first edge loses more accuracy than removing a weak op like pooling.
Deleting a strong conv edge into the output is more damaging than deleting a weak one.
Pooling already provides a usable path, so upgrading it to a conv gains less than filling a missing edge.
A skip on the direct input-to-output edge helps gradient flow when it was absent, but is a downgrade when the edge was a conv.
Replacing a 3x3 conv with a parameter-free skip loses capacity, a worse change than replacing a weak op.
Adding a conv to an empty edge gives a larger gain than swapping ops on an edge that already carries one.
